assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology enabled an exceptionally consequential therapeutic advance for diabetes and obesity.
assessment.attribution: Holst, Mojsov, and Drucker provide a coherent three-person account of core physiological discovery and its translation.
assessment.maturity: The biological mechanism and broad clinical benefit are mature and extensively established.
uncertainties: The contribution of drug-development leadership, including Lotte Bjerre Knudsen, creates a difficult but important attribution boundary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: CAR-T therapy established a new therapeutic modality with profound benefit in otherwise refractory cancers.
assessment.attribution: These three candidates represent major complementary contributions to engineered T-cell cancer therapy.
assessment.maturity: Durable clinical remissions and continuing expansion of the platform establish maturity.
uncertainties: Toxicity, access, and variable efficacy in solid tumors limit the universality of the intervention.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HPV virus-like-particle vaccination offers a powerful route to preventing infection-associated cancers.
assessment.attribution: Frazer, Lowy, and Schiller form a well-defined attribution set for the vaccine concept and its realization.
assessment.maturity: Its preventive effect, implementation, and public-health relevance are firmly demonstrated.
uncertainties: The full population-level effect on cancer incidence depends on coverage and long follow-up.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PCSK9 linked human genetics to a highly effective cholesterol-lowering target and major therapeutic class.
assessment.attribution: Hobbs, Cohen, and Seidah capture central genetic and molecular contributions, though the discovery history is broad.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism and clinical efficacy of PCSK9 inhibition are well established.
uncertainties: Catherine Boileau and Marianne Abifadel also have substantial claims to recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: CFTR modulators converted molecular understanding of cystic fibrosis into transformative mechanism-based treatment.
assessment.attribution: Welsh represents decisive CFTR physiology, while Van Goor and Negulescu represent critical therapeutic development.
assessment.maturity: Clinical benefit across eligible cystic-fibrosis populations is substantial and sustained.
uncertainties: The contribution of Jesús Tito González and Sabine Hadida complicates a three-person attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics fundamentally changed the capacity to test causal functions of specified cells in living systems.
assessment.attribution: Hegemann and Nagel are central to microbial opsin work, while Deisseroth was pivotal in establishing the experimental platform.
assessment.maturity: The method is widely validated and has reshaped experimental neuroscience and physiology.
uncertainties: Credit is distributed across several essential contributors, including Ernst Bamberg, Gero Miesenböck, and Edward S. Boyden.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing provided a landmark demonstration that RNA-targeted therapy can alter a lethal inherited disease.
assessment.attribution: Krainer and Bennett provide a concise pairing of splicing mechanism and antisense therapeutic development.
assessment.maturity: The therapeutic principle has achieved clear clinical validation in spinal muscular atrophy.
uncertainties: Long-term comparative outcomes across changing treatment strategies remain under evaluation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL inhibition established a defining model of molecularly targeted cancer treatment.
assessment.attribution: Lydon, Druker, and Sawyers represent drug discovery, clinical translation, and mechanistic development of the approach.
assessment.maturity: The durable clinical success of targeted BCR-ABL inhibition is unequivocal.
uncertainties: The foundational identification of BCR-ABL and the broader history of targeted oncology extend beyond the proposed credit set.
